nodes.title: Direction and strategy
nodes.body:
Where should we focus, and what will we decline?

Write the constraint and outcome. Compare at least two materially different paths and the status quo. Test the assumption most likely to change the choice. Allocate a bounded commitment and set a review trigger.

nodes.title: Organization and HR
nodes.body:
How should responsibilities, expectations, and people processes work?

Start with recurring work and decision bottlenecks. Map responsibilities and decision rights. Specify expected outcomes, support, escalation, and review cadence. Pilot a small change before a broad reorganization.

nodes.title: Hiring and selection
nodes.body:
Should we hire, for what outcomes, and whom?

Define role outcomes and essential entry competencies. Consider redesigning or stopping work before adding headcount. Set scoring anchors before seeing candidates. Run structured interviews and a bounded work sample. Compare independent evidence, resolve gaps, and document the decision.

nodes.title: People development
nodes.body:
How do we help people grow into more capable work?

Identify a concrete capability gap with the person. Check whether expectations, tools, time, or incentives explain it. Agree a practice task and support. Observe, discuss feedback, repeat, and evaluate transfer against baseline.

nodes.title: Product and engineering development
nodes.body:
What should we build, test, release, and maintain?

State the user problem and success measure. Identify the riskiest assumption. Select a small test or implementation slice. Define acceptance criteria, owner, dependency checks, and rollback before release. Review observed use and delivery estimates afterward.

nodes.title: Design workflows
nodes.body:
How do we move from user evidence to a tested experience?

Discover user context. Define the actual task and constraint. Explore multiple concepts. Test prototypes on representative tasks. Record observations separately from interpretations; revise and specify behavior, states, and acceptance checks for implementation.

nodes.title: Design ethos
nodes.body:
What principles make our work recognizably ours?

Collect examples of excellent and unacceptable experiences. Explain why. Draft a few principles tied to user needs. For each, specify a sacrifice, example, counterexample, and exception. Test them against conflicting real designs before adoption.

nodes.title: Brand and positioning
nodes.body:
What should buyers understand, believe, and remember about us?

Identify the buyer and actual alternatives. Connect distinctive capability to value. Choose a clear category and test comprehension. Translate the position into message hierarchy, verbal style, visual principles, and repeatable assets. Measure understanding and recall in context.

nodes.title: Market and customer learning
nodes.body:
Which audience, channel, or customer problem deserves more investment?

Write the hypothesis and current evidence. Choose an observation or bounded experiment that could disconfirm it. Define success and stop conditions in advance. Compare results with the baseline and record the next allocation decision.

nodes.title: Operations and partnerships
nodes.body:
How should recurring work, vendors, and agreements be managed?

Define the work and required service level. Compare available arrangements, including internal execution. Establish decision rights and fallback. Review dependencies and failure signals. Record commitments and a review date.
